<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XI.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|251}}</noinclude>goest thou thither againe? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, Are there not tvvelue houres of the day? If a man vvalke in the day, he stumbleth not: because he seeth the light of this world: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10}}† but if he walke in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11}}† These things he said: and after this he saith to them, Lazarus our frende sleepeth: but I goe that I may raise him from sleepe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}}† His Disciples therfore said, Lord, if he sleepe, he shal be safe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}}† but {{sc|Iesvs}} spake of his death: & they thought that he spake c {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''de dormitione somni''.}}∷ of the sleeping of sleepe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}}† Then therfore {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them plainely, Lazarus is dead: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}}† and I am glad for your sake, that you may beleeue, because I vvas not there. but let vs goe to him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}}† Thomas therfore, vvho is called Didymus, said to his condisciples, Let vs also goe, to die vvith him.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore came, and found him novv hauing been foure daies in the graue. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}}† (and Bethánia vvas nigh to Hierusalem about fiftene furlonges.) {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}}† And many of the Ievves vvere come to Martha and Marie, to comfort them concerning theire brother. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}}† Martha therfore vvhen she heard that {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas come, vvent to meete him: but Marie sat at home. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in a Masse for the dead vpon the day of the burial or deposition.}}Martha therfore said to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Lord if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}}† but novv also I knovv that vvhat things soeuer thou shalt aske of God, God vvil giue thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to her, Thy brother shal rise againe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}}† Martha saith to him, I knovv that he shal rise againe in the resurrection, in the last day. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=25}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to her, I am the resurrection and the life: he that beleeueth in me, although he be dead, shal liue. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=26}}† and euery one that liueth, and beleeueth in me, shal not die for euer, Beleeuest thou this? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=27}}† She saith to him, Yea Lord, I haue beleeued that thou art {{sc|Christ}} the sonne of God that art come into this vvorld.⊣

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=28}}† And vvhen she had said these things, she vvent, and called Marie her sister secretely, saying, The maister is come, & calleth thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=29}}† She, when she heard, riseth quickely, & commeth to him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=30}}† For {{sc|Iesvs}} was not yet come into the towne: but he vvas yet in that place vvhere Martha had mette him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=31}}† The Ievves therfore that vvere vvith her in the house and did comfort her, vvhen they savv Marie that she rose quickly and vvent forth, folovved her, saying, That she goeth to the graue, to vveepe there. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=32}}† Marie therfore vvhen<noinclude>{{rh||Ii ij|she}}</noinclude>
